units.rhetorical_move: states two goals and one scope before any method
units.function: name the twin objective and the constraint first

original_instantiations: economic output and job satisfaction are maximized together
sustainability bounds the scope of both goals

units.source_excerpt: This paper presents a model to maximize both the economic output and job satisfaction.
units.reusable_pattern: Open by naming two objectives and the constraint that bounds them.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not drop the sustainability constraint.

units.rhetorical_move: credits the result to a named census file
units.function: tie the simulation to one cited dataset

original_instantiations: simulations run on one named census year
the optimal feasible solution comes out of that run

units.source_excerpt: We run simulations of the system with real-world census data to find the optimal feasible solution.
units.reusable_pattern: Attribute the solution to a simulation on one named dataset.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not name a dataset the text does not cite.

units.rhetorical_move: decomposes the problem into six numbered sub-problems
units.function: announce the decomposition before solving any part

original_instantiations: the problem splits into six sub-problems
each sub-problem gets its own ordinal paragraph

units.source_excerpt: To address the problem, we decompose it into six sub-problems.
units.reusable_pattern: State the number of sub-problems before describing any of them.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not renumber the six parts.

units.rhetorical_move: reports two optimal dollar figures
units.function: close a sub-problem on its numeric optimum

original_instantiations: the optimal minimum wage is one stated yearly sum
the optimal parental leave pay is a second stated sum

units.source_excerpt: We find that the optimal minimum wage is a stated sum per year.
units.reusable_pattern: Report an optimum as we find that followed by the figure.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not round the stated figures.

units.rhetorical_move: claims one objective does not hurt the others
units.function: deny a tradeoff the reader expects

original_instantiations: maximizing parental leave pay barely moves the minimum wage
average income stays nearly unchanged as well

units.source_excerpt: We find that maximizing the parental leave pay will not reduce the minimum wage significantly.
units.reusable_pattern: Deny an expected tradeoff with will not and significantly.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not turn the denial into a proof.

units.rhetorical_move: states a sustainable migration cadence
units.function: give the policy as a count per interval

original_instantiations: ten thousand migrants every ten years stay sustainable
the same cadence absorbs a large refugee wave

units.source_excerpt: Our model shows a strategy of migrants every ten years is sustainable.
units.reusable_pattern: State a policy as a count per time interval plus a sustainability claim.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not change the interval.

units.rhetorical_move: addresses the client by title
units.function: open the letter to a named office

original_instantiations: the director is addressed as honored
thanks for hiring precedes any recommendation

units.source_excerpt: Honored Director of LIFE, thank you for hiring and trusting us.
units.reusable_pattern: Open a policy letter by addressing the client by title and thanking them.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not invent a personal name for the director.

units.rhetorical_move: claims confidence from real data
units.function: ground confidence in the data source

original_instantiations: confidence rests on modeling plus simulation
the simulation uses real-world data

units.source_excerpt: Our recommendations are based on precise modeling and computer simulation based on real-world data.
units.reusable_pattern: Claim confidence only after naming the modeling and the data.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not claim confidence without the data clause.

units.rhetorical_move: gives one bolded recommendation per paragraph
units.function: lead each advice with a bold imperative

original_instantiations: each recommendation opens with a bold imperative
the justification follows in the same paragraph

units.source_excerpt: Select Educated Immigrants. We propose that LIFE recruit more immigrants who own a bachelor degree.
units.reusable_pattern: Lead a recommendation with a bold imperative, then justify it.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not add a recommendation heading the letter lacks.

units.rhetorical_move: calls a feared effect unnecessary
units.function: dismiss a concern in one clause

original_instantiations: concern about the minimum wage harming output is unnecessary
the change in average income is called negligible

units.source_excerpt: Concerns about the negative effect of a high minimum wage on GDP are unnecessary.
units.reusable_pattern: Dismiss a feared side effect as unnecessary, then call the change negligible.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not treat unnecessary as a measured result.

units.rhetorical_move: warns of a cascade from one weak generation
units.function: turn one shortfall into a chain reaction

original_instantiations: insufficient education in the first generation starts a cascade
the cascade ends in the downfall of the colony

units.source_excerpt: If education of the first generation is insufficient, chain reaction will lead to a cascade.
units.reusable_pattern: Warn with a conditional that ends in a cascade and a downfall.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not soften the downfall.

units.rhetorical_move: closes on a hope for the project
units.function: end the letter with a wish

original_instantiations: the close hopes the suggestions prove useful
the project is called a successful beginning

units.source_excerpt: We hope that our suggestions are useful and the project will be a successful beginning.
units.reusable_pattern: Close a policy letter on a hope verb and the project's name.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not read the hope as a forecast.

units.rhetorical_move: restates the six sub-problems as the plan
units.function: give the reader the decomposition a second time

original_instantiations: the introduction repeats the six-part plan
each part is named before its section

units.source_excerpt: We decompose the problem into the same six sub-problems in the introduction.
units.reusable_pattern: Restate the summary's decomposition once the letter is over.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not count the restatement as a new result.

units.rhetorical_move: names the three balancing factors
units.function: fix the scope as three named factors

original_instantiations: economy, education and equality are the three factors
sustainability frames all three

units.source_excerpt: We consider three important balancing factors: economy, education, and equality.
units.reusable_pattern: Name the factors in a colon list of exactly three.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not add a fourth factor.

units.rhetorical_move: builds parameters in three tiers
units.function: layer the variables from person to society

original_instantiations: parameters sit on individual, family and societal tiers
each tier carries income, education and equality

units.source_excerpt: There are three tiers of parameters, on individual level, family level and societal level.
units.reusable_pattern: Organize variables into tiers and name each tier.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not collapse the tiers.

units.rhetorical_move: says a derived index simplifies the tiers
units.function: justify a new index by simplification

original_instantiations: the index system simplifies the three-tier parameters
it also tries to reveal dependency among them

units.source_excerpt: To simplify the three-tier basic parameter, we design a comprehensive index system.
units.reusable_pattern: Introduce a derived index as a simplification of the raw tiers.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not claim the index removes information.

units.rhetorical_move: names the census file and its size
units.function: state the source and the row count together

original_instantiations: one census release supplies every row we use
its year and its size are named together

units.source_excerpt: We extract data from the PUMS database of more than a million citizens.
units.reusable_pattern: Name the database and its size in one sentence.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not round the row count away.

units.rhetorical_move: compares the selected group with a random draw
units.function: set a baseline sample beside the chosen one

original_instantiations: an equal-sized draw stands beside the chosen group
the chosen group then shows a clear edge

units.source_excerpt: In comparison to the selected group, we generate a random sample of the same size.
units.reusable_pattern: Compare the chosen group against a random sample of equal size.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not skip the baseline.

units.rhetorical_move: reports the advantage without a test statistic
units.function: claim an obvious advantage in plain words

original_instantiations: the chosen cohort holds a plain, untested edge
no statistic is attached to that edge

units.source_excerpt: The selected group shows an obvious advantage in building a successful society.
units.reusable_pattern: State an advantage as obvious rather than as a test result.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not invent a significance test.

units.rhetorical_move: glosses a negative rate as a bad condition
units.function: translate a sign into a plain-language state

original_instantiations: a negative saving rate means income cannot meet expenditure
the person is then said to be in bad condition

units.source_excerpt: A negative saving rate indicates that his income cannot meet his expenditure, thus in bad condition.
units.reusable_pattern: Gloss the sign of a rate in everyday words.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not leave the gloss out.

units.rhetorical_move: reports the consistency ratio beside the eigenvalue
units.function: give both the eigenvalue and the ratio

original_instantiations: the maximum eigenvalue is stated to four decimals
the consistency ratio is stated and said to pass

units.source_excerpt: The maximum eigenvalue is stated and the consistency ratio meets the requirement.
units.reusable_pattern: Report an eigenvalue and its consistency ratio together.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not drop the ratio.

units.rhetorical_move: states death as a logistic of age
units.function: give mortality as one named function

original_instantiations: death probability is a logistic function of age
the midpoint of the curve is a stated age

units.source_excerpt: Residents only die off naturally, and the death probability is a logistic function of age.
units.reusable_pattern: Define mortality as a named function of one variable.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not add causes of death the assumption excludes.

units.rhetorical_move: sets the unemployment rate by citation
units.function: anchor a constant to a cited source

original_instantiations: the unemployment rate is set at a stated percent
the percent is credited to a cited estimation method

units.source_excerpt: We set the unemployment rate at a stated percent according to a cited estimation method.
units.reusable_pattern: Justify a fixed rate by naming who estimated it.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not present the rate as measured here.

units.rhetorical_move: calls the tax rate reasonable by citation
units.function: defend a constant as reasonable

original_instantiations: the tax rate is set at a stated fraction
the fraction is called reasonable by a citation

units.source_excerpt: We set the tax rate at a stated fraction, a reasonable number according to a cited source.
units.reusable_pattern: Defend a chosen constant as reasonable and cite the source.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not treat reasonable as derived.

units.rhetorical_move: divides families into five named classes
units.function: bin the population and give each bin an income

original_instantiations: families fall into five economic classes
each class gets an income and a proportion

units.source_excerpt: The city of families is divided into five economic brackets according to their condition.
units.reusable_pattern: Partition the population into named classes with an income each.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not merge two classes.

units.rhetorical_move: states three objectives in one sentence
units.function: name the maximize and the minimize together

original_instantiations: minimum wage and average income are to be increased
the standard deviation is to be decreased

units.source_excerpt: Our objective is to increase the minimum wage and average income, but decrease the standard deviation.
units.reusable_pattern: State opposing objectives in one sentence joined by but.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not drop the decrease.

units.rhetorical_move: links people who share occupation and education
units.function: define an edge by a shared attribute

original_instantiations: same occupation and education create an immediate link
a shared pair of parents adds an edge too

units.source_excerpt: Residents and immigrants of the same occupation and education level establish an immediate relationship.
units.reusable_pattern: Define a network edge by a shared attribute.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not add edge rules the text lacks.

units.rhetorical_move: reads a high degree as wealth
units.function: turn a graph statistic into a social claim

original_instantiations: a high degree node is assumed financially well off
a high average degree makes the society wealthy

units.source_excerpt: We assume that an individual with high degree is in good financial condition.
units.reusable_pattern: Gloss a network statistic as a social condition, and mark it as an assumption.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not present the gloss as a result.

units.rhetorical_move: solves the objectives with a named algorithm
units.function: credit the optimum to one algorithm

original_instantiations: the three objectives are solved by one named algorithm
the algorithm is named in full

units.source_excerpt: We solve the three-objective optimization problem by a named elite genetic algorithm.
units.reusable_pattern: Attribute an optimum to one named algorithm.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not substitute a different algorithm.

units.rhetorical_move: compares two migration options
units.function: declare one option better on two measures

original_instantiations: option one beats option two on population
the same option also beats it on output

units.source_excerpt: We find that option one is much better than option two both on population and on output.
units.reusable_pattern: Compare two named options and say which wins on which measures.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not add a third option.

units.rhetorical_move: gives two reasons for the winner
units.function: support the comparison with a numbered pair

original_instantiations: the first reason is a shorter generational gap
the second reason is a shortage of jobs

units.source_excerpt: There are two reasons. One is the shorter gap, the other is the shortage of jobs.
units.reusable_pattern: Follow a comparison with exactly two reasons.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not add a third reason.

units.rhetorical_move: excludes children from the migrant wave
units.function: state who is left out and why

original_instantiations: no children under a stated age join the wave
the reason given is the danger of the trip

units.source_excerpt: No children under a stated age are included, for it is too dangerous to bring them.
units.reusable_pattern: Exclude a group and give the reason in a for clause.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not omit the reason.

units.rhetorical_move: tests robustness by adding noise
units.function: perturb the inputs and report mean and spread

original_instantiations: noise is added to the initial values
mean and standard deviation are reported over many runs

units.source_excerpt: To testify the robustness, we add noise to initial values and report the mean and standard deviation.
units.reusable_pattern: Test robustness by adding noise and reporting both mean and spread.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not report only the mean.

units.rhetorical_move: fixes the unbiased baseline in the caption
units.function: state the unperturbed values beside the test

original_instantiations: the caption lists the unbiased parameter values
the run count and the year are stated too

units.source_excerpt: The table states the unbiased parameters and the number of independent runs.
units.reusable_pattern: Put the baseline values in the caption of the robustness table.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not separate the baseline from the table.

units.rhetorical_move: lists strengths as bullets
units.function: give each strength its own bullet

original_instantiations: each strength is one bullet
the first credits the number of parameters

units.source_excerpt: We take a lot of basic and derived parameters into consideration and establish a comprehensive system.
units.reusable_pattern: Write each strength as a separate bullet beginning with we.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not merge two strengths into one bullet.

units.rhetorical_move: says the model evolves like the real world
units.function: claim realism from the number of subsystems

original_instantiations: seven named subsystems make up the model
the model is said to evolve like the real world

units.source_excerpt: This model evolves like our real world because it consists of many named systems.
units.reusable_pattern: Claim realism by listing the subsystems first.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not claim realism without the list.

units.rhetorical_move: says the model was built to be adjustable
units.function: claim extensibility as an intention

original_instantiations: the model was intentionally made easy to adjust
future research topics are named as the reason

units.source_excerpt: We intentionally make our model easy to adjust to further research requirements.
units.reusable_pattern: Claim extensibility by saying it was intentional.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not present the extensibility as already done.

units.rhetorical_move: admits parameters were set subjectively
units.function: name the cause of the weakness

original_instantiations: some parameter values are determined subjectively
no related essays could be found to refer to

units.source_excerpt: The values of some parameters are determined subjectively, since we cannot find related essays.
units.reusable_pattern: Admit a subjective choice and give the missing source as the cause.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not hide the subjectivity.

units.rhetorical_move: admits results may not repeat
units.function: limit the claim to this database

original_instantiations: part of the database is computer generated
results may not be repeated on other databases

units.source_excerpt: Some results may not be repeated on other databases, even though the database is quite large.
units.reusable_pattern: Concede that results may not repeat, then note the database is already large.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not claim the results are reproducible.

units.rhetorical_move: admits one omitted mechanism
units.function: name what the model leaves out and when it matters

original_instantiations: job competition is ignored in the job system
the omission is tolerable short term but fails long term

units.source_excerpt: We ignore the job competition, reasonable in the short term but failing in the long run.
units.reusable_pattern: Admit an omission and bound it to the short term.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not extend the omission past the stated bound.

units.rhetorical_move: breaks a web address across lines
units.function: keep the citation's line break

original_instantiations: one census address is split after a dot
the citation otherwise names the bureau

units.source_excerpt: The census address is broken across two lines after the dot.
units.reusable_pattern: Leave a citation's broken address unrepaired.
prohibited_generalizations: The broken address belongs to this reference list and does not transfer.

units.rhetorical_move: prints the initialization as commented code
units.function: let the code carry its own comments

original_instantiations: each block of code opens with a percent comment
the comment names the flag being initialized

units.source_excerpt: The code initializes each flag under a comment that names it.
units.reusable_pattern: Present initialization code with a comment naming each flag.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not strip the comments.

units.rhetorical_move: keeps the misspelled comment
units.function: leave the code's typos in place

original_instantiations: initialize is spelled three different ways in the comments
the typos mark one author

units.source_excerpt: The comments spell initialize in more than one way.
units.reusable_pattern: Keep a repeated comment typo as evidence of one hand.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not correct the comment when citing it.

units.rhetorical_move: guards a draw inside a loop
units.function: show the code rejecting an out-of-range draw

original_instantiations: a drawn value is rejected when it falls outside the range
the draw repeats until it lands inside

units.source_excerpt: The code redraws a value while it falls outside the allowed range.
units.reusable_pattern: Show a guard that repeats a random draw until it is in range.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not remove the guard.
